entries:
Alpha 1.79.16 (worn masonry, woodland shading and shared enemy rendering)

  • The First Grove vault follows a curved stone profile with shallow carved lips on both faces. Its original overhead clearance, footprint, depth and shared fieldstone material remain unchanged.
  • Grove and Bastion pier courses have worn corners and staggered masonry joints instead of monolithic slices. Existing material batching is retained; no new textures or runtime draw buckets are added.
  • Natural stone gains continuous mineral grain, sheltered lichen and damp lower courses. Detail follows world space across curved faces and fades below pixel size rather than painting another brick grid over the vault.
  • Nearby Skeletons share opaque render batches across their independently animated rigs, reducing repeated color and shadow draws without removing enemies or changing their surfaces, animations or hitboxes. Supplied class models and unreviewed enemy families keep their existing rendering path.
  • Bent woodland leaves have continuous lighting across their sections and subtle plant-to-plant tones instead of identical repeated colors. Existing plants, silhouettes, triangle counts, placements, wind and walking clearances remain unchanged.
  • Area cleanup releases each instanced mesh's matrix and color buffers as well as its shared geometry, preventing those owned GPU buffers from accumulating across area changes.
  • Collision, paths, quest targets, planted roots, thresholds and gameplay rules stay unchanged. Original geometry and scene performance limits remain required.
  • This is incremental landmark refinement, not final modern-world approval, equipped-party or physical-device qualification, the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, currency or permission change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.15 (scenery rendering and atlas detail)

  • Owned, unchanged scene containers and foliage groups avoid repeated local matrix composition and unnecessary static world-matrix multiplication. Actors, bones, equipment animations, moved parents and reparented scenery remain live.
  • The foliage registry visits registered scenery instead of unrelated character rigs and buildings. Cell bounds and frustum results are reused only for exact current transforms, bounds, camera, light and shadow-filter inputs. No movement thresholds or timed approximations are introduced.
  • Irrelevant direct foliage cells skip eligibility work, while nested scenery and live region, material and visibility changes retain their existing behavior. Pointer targeting reuses each actor's owned interaction box instead of repeatedly searching its fitted rig; detached or replaced boxes fall back to normal lookup.
  • Ordinary world frames no longer search the entire scene for a casino interior that is not present. Casino doors and floors reuse their current owned scene roots, reacquire replacements and release references on cleanup. Seating, floor visibility, table timers and wagers are unchanged.
  • The atlas uses distinct engraved birch, pine, willow, deadwood, briar, wind-bent cypress and storm-crystal symbols at their existing world locations. Roads, gates, destinations, phone controls and cached map sizes are unchanged.
  • Generated groundcover keeps its fixed local transform while shader wind and live instance transforms remain active. Detached scenery and disposed renderers restore their original methods and remove owned listeners.
  • Geometry, density, shadows, cell sizes, filter margins, quality settings, collisions, gameplay and frame budgets remain unchanged. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world; final equipped-party, device, modern-art and feature-freeze qualification remain open.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, economy or permission change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.14 (character surfaces and constructed dungeon interiors)

  • All 252 supplied wearable fits now have registered High/Low detail selections. Reduced copies preserve source identities, rigging and fit; 32 unchanged variants reuse originals. Missing copies fall back to the registered original and record the affected slot. Supplied source assets remain unchanged.
  • Supplied equipment gains shared cloth, leather, wood and metal surface detail while preserving authored textures, colors and magical accents. Only eligible materials with usable UVs receive the generated maps; compatible equipment still batches together.
  • Robes and skirts hide enclosed underwear and body hips. Robes also mask fully concealed upper trouser armor without removing visible lower legs, crossing triangles or exposed skirt waistbands. Outfit changes restore the original layers; supplied GLBs and other characters are unchanged.
  • The game world and character preview now share filmic highlight handling. Existing lighting, exposure, quality controls and passes are retained.
  • Dungeon vigils have stepped feet, profiled shafts and forged cages; reliquary coffers gain vaulted lids and straps, and restorative fonts have hollow basins. Existing shared materials and room batching are reused.
  • All five dungeon themes have varied, worn flagstones with registered physical surface detail. Compact room markers leave the combat floor readable while preserving objective, reward, cleared-room and exit feedback. Floors stay flat; collisions, layout, encounter and reward rules are unchanged.
  • This is an integrated polish pass, not final modern-art approval or the 1.80 feature freeze. Raised terrain, equipped-party/device qualification and full 1.87 remain staged. No account wipe, schema migration or economy change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.13 (optional public outage monitoring)

  • The existing outage monitor can optionally check the public login page, frontend release manifest and backend health over normal HTTPS, in addition to its local API and database check.
  • Public checks require matching frontend/backend/local release identities and a ready database, with bounded response sizes, one shared public deadline and no redirects or forced IPv4. These checks verify HTTP structure, not full browser gameplay or off-machine coverage.
  • Both public endpoint settings default to empty. Paired configuration is checked before replacing the game service; invalid or incomplete public settings fail closed. Existing installed monitoring remains local-only until an operator explicitly configures and restarts the matching monitor artifact.
  • The existing alert recipients, three-failure/two-success debounce, reminder limits, email provider and retention remain unchanged. The operator guide explains same-artifact rollback and release-transition qualification before enabling public alerts.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, retention, economy, quest or Dark Realm access changes. Full 1.80 freeze, operations ownership, off-machine backup, modern-art and beta gates remain open. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.12 (administrator maintenance and incident notices)

  • Admins can prepare maintenance, incident-update and recovery notices in Administration, review the exact public text and explicitly send it to connected players across all areas.
  • Notices require current durable administrator authority and successful activity storage, checked again before queueing. Plain text, UTC update times, bounded requests and the existing activity retention protect this route.
  • Missing acknowledgements never resend automatically. History records admission only, not guaranteed delivery; disconnected players do not receive old transient notices.
  • The operator guide includes safe incident triage, communication, escalation and reopening procedures. This tool does not stop the game, restart services, send email or change player progress.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, retention, economy, quest or Dark Realm access changes. Original 1.80 feature-freeze and full modern-art, operations and beta gates remain open. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.11 (elemental landscapes and mineral formations)

  • World entry downloads a consolidated game engine instead of hundreds of separate game modules. Login still loads independently; shared session state, gameplay class names, original editable sources and release-versioned assets are preserved.
  • Startup failures retain a non-sensitive phase and category for diagnostics, without exposing raw errors or account details. Interrupted module downloads and incompatible module exports now recommend reloading the page. This is recovery guidance, not automatic retries or a claim that every startup failure is resolved.
  • If WebGL 2 is unavailable or blocked, entering the world returns to login with hardware-acceleration and browser/device guidance. The message appears in the page, never a browser alert. Successful renderer creation and browser security settings are unchanged.
  • Login now shows only the latest ten patch notes. Load more notes fetches the next ten on demand; the complete history is retained. Login startup no longer waits for the full game-engine dependency graph and also initializes if the document-ready event has already fired.
  • Fixed Firefox login startup: register the dependency import map before loading any modules, while preserving private recovery-link scrubbing before analytics starts.
  • Water and Air conifers have layered needle boughs instead of solid cones. Drowned willows have folded leaves and hanging shoots; Fire snags have connected crooked branches and attached ember tips.
  • Fire and Air mineral formations have asymmetric facets, weathered basalt/slate detail and grounded side forks instead of floating fragments. Water and Air conductor shards share the refined mineral shape.
  • The existing 180 Water, 165 Fire and 165 Air scenery objects form uneven stands beside travel routes. Tree counts, per-tree scales and rotations, Earth placements, walking lanes, hazards and investigation clearings are retained.
  • Air landmark edges gain leafy heath: 1,111 plants on High and 617 on Low. This is new visual-only scenery, with no movement blockers. Switching graphics quality now updates regional crowns and all 24 groundcover beds without reloading, releases old buffers and preserves material ownership.
  • Original scene performance limits remain required. This is regional component polish, not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. Raised terrain, wearable derivatives and broader renderer optimizations remain staged; landscape cohesion and sparse travel stretches remain work in progress.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, quests, combat, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.10 (forest floor and willow silhouettes)

  • Earth soil and forest litter have less obvious texture repetition. Moss detail is filtered at distance to reduce speckling while retaining the existing paths and ground-cover fields.
  • Mourning willows have curved hanging shoots and narrow leaves instead of reusing rounded birch foliage for their three curtains. All 256 leaves and existing High/Low triangle budgets, placements and walking clearances remain.
  • Fixed lighting on tilted woodland parts: their exact static transform is baked once so instanced normals remain correct. Geometry silhouettes, material ownership, shadows and quality switches are preserved; no additional tree parts or draw calls.
  • Raised-terrain preview rocks have narrower, varied shoulders and gentle fractures within their existing collision footprints. This is preview preparation: raised terrain remains disabled in ordinary public worlds. Wearable derivatives and broader renderer changes remain staged.
  • Future hosted browser installations have a 15-minute deadline, so stalled downloads fail visibly instead of blocking deployment for hours. All release test gates remain required.
  • Server, outage monitor, CI and isolated QA builds now use Go 1.27.2, fixing the newly reported reachable standard-library security issues. Dependency versions, vulnerability checks and deployment gates are unchanged.
  • Not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. No account wipe, schema migration, quests, combat, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.9 (woodland bark and natural undergrowth)

  • Earth-realm birch, pine and willow now have distinct bark: broken birch markings and peeling, coarse pine ridges and finer willow grain. Surface color, roughness and filtered relief follow the existing trunks instead of sharing generic timber.
  • Gloamwood grass and ferns form uneven stands with clearer gaps rather than a uniformly jittered grid. Every existing plant, species, scale and rotation is retained, with the same Low-quality subset. Roads, town approaches and investigation sites retain their walking clearances.
  • No new textures, lights or collision footprints. Tree placement, geometry, wind and shadows are unchanged. This is a woodland component improvement, not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. Raised terrain, wearable derivatives and additional renderer optimizations remain staged.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, combat, quests, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.8 (woodland foliage and cleaner UI startup)

  • Gloamwood pines have fuller hanging needle fans with varied height and stronger folds. Woodland sedge has curved, gently twisted leaves, varied blade widths and a greener palette instead of uniform flat ribbons.
  • The refinements retain every plant and tree, existing High/Low triangle counts, wind, lighting, shadows and collision footprints. Fuller pine fans stay inside the original crown-height envelope. They improve the existing code-owned woodland, not the whole-world composition or final modern-art milestone.
  • Published UI styles now load as one ordered stylesheet instead of forty separate requests. The same desktop and phone cascade, local fonts and startup recovery remain; source styles stay modular. This reduces startup requests, but does not guarantee recovery from every network failure.
  • This is not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain, wearable derivatives and additional renderer optimizations remain staged. No account wipe, schema migration, gameplay, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.7 (Earth surface refinement)

  • Gloamwood soil now has more coherent aggregate detail, with restrained damp-crevice and dry-face colors. Moss cushions use a separate broad field and retain sheltered woodland variation instead of blending every ground layer into one muddy wash.
  • The prepared rock material for staged raised terrain has bedding that is gently inclined and broken by weathering rather than embossed into contour-like lines. This does not activate the raised-world rocks. Existing geometry, collision footprints, roads, plants, lights and shadows remain unchanged; the refinement adds no meshes, textures or shader texture fetches.
  • This is a modest surface pass, not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. Raised terrain and wearable derivatives remain staged, not enabled by this patch. Air-realm canvas was already delivered in 1.79.3 and is unchanged here.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, quest, economy, combat or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.
